Regulation: B.C. Reg. 100/2026
Made under: Sustainable Environment Fund Act
Published in: No. 12 – B.C. Regs. 99 to 109, June 30, 2026
Deposit date: June 19, 2026

B.C. Reg. 100/2026, deposited June 19, 2026, under theSUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENT FUND ACT[section 6]. Order in Council 252/2026, approved and ordered June 19, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective July 1, 2026, the Sustainable Environment Fund Revenue Regulation, B.C. Reg. 142/2011, is repealed and the attached Sustainable Environment Fund Regulation is made. — T. DAVIDSON,Minister of Environment and Parks; D. GIBSON,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENT  FUND REGULATION 1This regulation prescribes, for the purposes of section 4 (g) of theSustainable Environment Fund Act, revenue derived under the following Acts: (a)Environmental Management Act; (b)Integrated Pest Management Act. Revenue underEnvironmental Management Act 2In respect of theEnvironmental Management Act, the prescribed revenue is all revenue that the government derives from any of the following under that Act: (a)	application fees and annual charges for approved waste management plans; (b)	application fees and annual charges for registrations under section 3[registration requirements]of the Asphalt Plant Regulation, B.C. Reg. 217/97; (c)	application fees and annual charges for operational certificates; (d)	fees under Part 4[Fees]of the Contaminated Sites Regulation, B.C. Reg. 375/96; (e)	application fees and annual charges for registrations under Division 2[Registration]of Part 2[Initial Administrative Requirements]of the Municipal Wastewater Regulation, B.C. Reg. 87/2012; (f)	annual charges for authorizations to discharge under the Oil and Gas Waste Regulation, B.C. Reg. 254/2005; (g)	annual charges for registrations under section 4[exemption from section 6 (2) and (3) of Act by compliance with code of practice]of the Waste Discharge Regulation, B.C. Reg. 320/2004. Revenue underIntegrated Pest Management Act 3In respect of theIntegrated Pest Management Act, the prescribed revenue is all revenue that the government derives from any of the following under that Act: (a)	fees for licences under section 4[licence for sale or use of pesticides]; (b)	fees for certificates under section 5[certificate for sale or use of pesticides by individuals];

minutes_briefs.title: B.C. updates Sustainable Environment Fund revenue rules, effective July 1, 2026
minutes_briefs.summary: B.C. has replaced its old Sustainable Environment Fund Revenue Regulation with a new one, effective July 1, 2026. The new regulation lists the specific fees and charges that count as revenue for the fund, including application fees for waste management plans, operational certificates, and pesticide licences. This change clarifies which payments go into the fund but does not change the fee amounts themselves.
minutes_briefs.action_required: No immediate action needed—just be aware that your fees now support the Sustainable Environment Fund under the updated regulation.

key_dates.label: New Sustainable Environment Fund Regulation takes effect (BC)
